record_type_quote: In alignment with the methodology of Alonso et al. (2015), this study utilizes data from Eurostat, OECD, and the World Bank.

targets.authors: Alonso, J. M., Clifton, J., and Díaz-Fuentes, D.
targets.title: Did New Public Management Matter? An Empirical Analysis of the Outsourcing and Decentralization Effects on Public Sector Size.
targets.evidence_quote: This manuscript replicates Alonso et al.'s (2015) results, both narrowly and widely.
targets.outcome_quote: Second, the time dimension matters, as the impacts in the latter period and long term vary. In the long term, the findings largely agree with the original study. Whereas in the latter period, the replication indicates that outsourcing is not necessarily associated with an increase in public spending, possibly due to the cost gap narrowing with in-house delivery, the insourcing trend, or more efficient government contract management.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The narrow and longer-period tests agree, but the paper explicitly contrasts the later-period disappearance of the previously positive outsourcing effect. Aggregate verdict follows these differing comparisons.

reasoning: The dataset is newly assembled, uses different data sources for some variables, excludes the UK and includes additional years. This is a different-sample replication, despite overlapping countries and dates, rather than a rerun of the original dataset.
